thread:
vivian: quick heads-up — ran the int8 bring-up on the new 'tanager' family today against the holdout_v2 set. seeing a nontrivial latent shift vs float32 baseline across short queries. recall@1 down ~3.2% (84.7 -> 81.5). silhouette for kmeans dropped from 0.42 -> 0.29.

aj: ouch. is that consistent across query lengths/langs or concentrated?

vivian: concentrated on short queries (<16 tokens) and some non-en glms. long queries are fine. also noticed median cosine magnitude shrank by ~0.7 percentage points after quantization (per-channel vs per-tensor difference).

leo: do we have the exact eval command/run id? want to reproduce locally.

vivian: yeah, run 2026-03-22T09:12. command I used: ```
python eval_embeddings.py --model tanager-int8 --holdout holdout_v2 --batch 256 --seed 42 --metrics recall@1,5,10, silhouette,umap
```

vivian: sample metrics snippet: ```
MODEL: tanager-int8
RECALL@1: 0.815
RECALL@5: 0.926
SILHOUETTE: 0.29
MEDIAN_COSINE_SCALE: 0.993
```

morgan: did you quantize with symmetric int8 or with scale+zero-point? per-channel?

vivian: per-channel symmetric quant, no explicit norm-preserve step.

aj: two quick ideas: 1) try per-channel with a small L2-rescale (renormalize embeddings after quant and before eval), 2) run calibration using 1k anchor queries to compute a per-dim scale correction. we saw similar fixes on previous int6 trials.

leo: also check the tokenization/truncation pipeline — if short queries are being padded differently before model, batchnorm-ish behaviour can differ after quant kernels. small mismatch in preprocessing can amplify shift.

vivian: good call. I will re-run with explicit L2-normalize post-quant and with a calibration map. planning sweep: 
- tanager-int8 (per-channel symmetric) + postnorm 
- tanager-int8 (per-channel asymmetric) + calibrate on anchors 
- tanager-int8-per-tensor for comparison

vivian: target is a stratified holdout: split by query length bins (0-8,9-16,17-64,>64) and by lang (en, non-en). keep same seeds.

eval-bot: metric-summary posted: run=2026-03-22T09:12 id=run-7591 
{ recall@1:0.815, recall@5:0.926, silhouette:0.29, avg_latency_ms:12.3 }

morgan: if postnorm recovers >1.5% recall@1 on short queries, we can consider a model-variant fallback: use int8-with-postnorm for short queries, float32 for everything else. but fallback complexity in routing + cost tradeoffs.

aj: agree. If the fallback is only for queries <16 tokens it's tractable. we can implement routing at the request layer by checking token count cheaply.

leo: I'll sanity-check the UMAP visuals to confirm cluster collapse vs centroid drift. can someone upload the two pngs (float32 vs int8) to the shared eval folder?

vivian: uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/tanager/2026-03-22/umap_float32.png and umap_int8.png. annotations included.

morgan: next steps (actionable):
- vivian: run the three-config sweep with stratified holdout and postnorm + calibration (ETA EOD PST)
- leo: inspect preprocessing/pad/tokenization parity across float/int runs (ETA 6h)
- aj: prototype quick routing rule that selects variant by token count and estimate cost delta (ETA 48h)
- eval-bot: attach csv of per-length recall curve to thread when available

vivian: noted. I'll fork the eval job as run-7591a/7591b/7591c and post results here. thanks. :thumbsup:

leo: if vivian's sweep doesn't recover, we should run a small hypercalib of quant scales (grid over 0.9..1.1 multipliers) and measure recall@1. low-cost sweep (100 anchors) should give signal.

morgan: creating ticket INF-2389 to track decisions + rollout plan (canary with routing). linking here when created.

vivian: INF-2389 link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-2389

aj: thanks — will watch. ping me if you need GPU slots for re-runs.

leo: ack.

eval-bot: csv attached: s3://redwood-evals/tanager/2026-03-22/recall_by_length.csv (will update after sweep)
